HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Sanskrit word Panch mean in Panch Mahabhoot? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Ten
   C. Five
   D. Seven

2. Which time of day is best for watering plants? (1 mark)
   A. Any time in the hottest sun
   B. Noon
   C. Midnight
   D. Early morning or evening

3. Which is the most famous sacred river in Hindu teaching? (1 mark)
   A. Ganga
   B. Nzoia
   C. Athi
   D. Tana

4. Which Jain teacher is linked with the bank of the Rijubalika river? (1 mark)
   A. Lord Mahavir
   B. Prahlad
   C. Guru Nanak
   D. Valmiki

5. Which Enlightened Being is a Sikh Guru? (1 mark)
   A. Lord Buddha
   B. Narsimha
   C. Sri Guru Ram Das Ji
   D. Parshvanath

6. What does Lord Narsimha look like? (1 mark)
   A. A man's body with a lion's head and claws
   B. A bird
   C. A snake
   D. A fish

7. Which city did Guru Ram Das Ji start? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Varanasi
   C. Nairobi
   D. Mombasa

8. What did Siddhartha later become? (1 mark)
   A. The Buddha, the Awakened One
   B. A Jain Tirthankar
   C. An Avtar of Vishnu
   D. A Sikh Guru

9. What do Sikhs eat together in the gurdwara? (1 mark)
   A. Langar, the community meal
   B. Prasad only from a priest
   C. Fasting food
   D. Nothing

10. Which action follows a Sikh teaching? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing lunch with someone who has none
   B. Teasing the child
   C. Hiding your lunch
   D. Keeping it all

11. Which is a main message of Jain scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Be greedy
   B. Practise pride
   C. Practise Ahimsa
   D. Take revenge

12. Which action follows the Jain teaching of gentleness? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking eggs
   B. Chasing animals
   C. Not stepping on ants or hurting animals for fun
   D. Throwing stones

13. What is Ayodhya Kaand about? (1 mark)
   A. The life of Guru Nanak
   B. The birth of the Buddha
   C. Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   D. Yoga

14. What is the Dhammapada? (1 mark)
   A. A list of temples
   B. A book of maps
   C. A book of wise sayings and verses
   D. A long story of a king

15. In which script is Guru Granth Sahib Ji written? (1 mark)
   A. Roman
   B. Gurmukhi
   C. Swahili script
   D. Arabic

16. How can you learn more about scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore them
   B. Keep them in a bag
   C. Copy them from memory only
   D. Listen to a resource person or visit a library

17. For how many years was Ram asked to live in the forest? (1 mark)
   A. Fourteen
   B. Five
   C. Two
   D. Fifty

18. What does Dainik mean? (1 mark)
   A. Weekly
   B. Monthly
   C. Yearly
   D. Daily

19. What is a good posture for prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Eat snacks
   B. Lie down and talk
   C. Sit calmly with hands folded
   D. Jump around

20. What is a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A Hindu place of worship
   C. A school
   D. A market

21. What does pita mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Father
   B. Friend
   C. Mother
   D. Wealth

22. Which goddess is Saraswati? (1 mark)
   A. Goddess of the river Ganga
   B. Goddess of war
   C. Goddess of knowledge and learning
   D. Goddess of fire

23. Which faith's story in the lesson is about truth and a king? (1 mark)
   A. Buddhism
   B. Jainism
   C. Hinduism
   D. Sikhism

24. What should you do if you find an item left on the vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. Give it away
   B. Give it to the driver or conductor
   C. Throw it away
   D. Keep it

25. Which two of the Buddha's five precepts appear in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Not to steal and not to lie
   B. Not to run and not to sing
   C. Not to swim and not to sit
   D. Not to sleep and not to eat

26. What does Asteya include besides not stealing things? (1 mark)
   A. Not using another's time or ideas without asking
   B. Not smiling
   C. Not walking
   D. Not eating

27. Who was Bhai Lalo? (1 mark)
   A. A king of Ayodhya
   B. A shopkeeper in Nairobi
   C. An honest carpenter in the Guru Nanak story
   D. A Jain monk

28. In Sasankasana, where do you rest your forehead? (1 mark)
   A. On your knees
   B. On the mat
   C. On the wall
   D. On a chair

29. In Sasankasana, where do your arms go at the end? (1 mark)
   A. On your head
   B. In the air
   C. Stretched forward on the floor
   D. Behind your back

30. How should the back be in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. Straight
   B. Twisted
   C. Bent
   D. Round

31. What is Paryushan Parva mainly about? (1 mark)
   A. Feasts only
   B. Racing
   C. Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   D. Wealth

32. Which teaching of Paryushan do children practise when they forgive a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Forgiveness
   C. Revenge
   D. Pride

33. In which months of the usual calendar does Maha Shivratri usually fall? (1 mark)
   A. December or January
   B. July or August
   C. October or November
   D. February or March

34. What does Micchami Dukkadam mean? (1 mark)
   A. Good morning
   B. May any harm I did be forgiven
   C. Thank you for the food
   D. Happy birthday

35. Why do the dates of Maha Shivratri and Paryushan change on the usual calendar? (1 mark)
   A. They follow the Moon
   B. They follow the shops
   C. They follow the market days
   D. They follow the school terms

36. What does charity work at festivals help with? (1 mark)
   A. Buying more sweets for ourselves
   B. Wasting food
   C. Making noise
   D. Sharing with those who cannot afford food or clothes

37. Guru (Brihaspati) is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Mars
   B. Jupiter
   C. Venus
   D. Saturn

38. What is the Indian name for Sunday? (1 mark)
   A. Somvaar
   B. Ravivaar
   C. Mangalvaar
   D. Shanivaar

39. Which planet is closest to the Sun? (1 mark)
   A. Mercury
   B. Mars
   C. Venus
   D. Saturn

40. Which activity helps you learn the days and planets? (1 mark)
   A. Painting
   B. Hiding the calendar
   C. Copying from a book
   D. Making a decorated calendar

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why are Enlightened Beings considered inspiring? Use two examples. (5 marks)

42. What does Dainik Prarthana mean? (2 marks)

43. Explain how the story of Prahlad shows faith in Paramatma. (3 marks)

44. Describe how to sit in Vajra Asana. (3 marks)

45. Write three main teachings of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. (3 marks)

46. Describe the story of Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo and its lesson. (4 marks)

47. Match the days to the heavenly bodies: Ravivaar, Somvaar, Mangalvaar. (3 marks)

48. Write the seven days of the week in the Indian traditional calendar with their heavenly bodies. (4 marks)

49. Write three ways of conserving water in the community. (3 marks)

50. Name two grahas in the traditional calendar that are not planets in modern science. (2 marks)

51. Name the two Ramayan kaands studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

52. Explain four lessons we learn from the Ramayan. (4 marks)

53. Describe an experiment to show that plants need water. (4 marks)

54. Discuss how people of different faiths show respect for water and trees. (5 marks)

55. List four facts about the planets linked with the days. (4 marks)

56. Explain how to say the Gayatri Mantra correctly. (3 marks)

57. Suggest four activities for celebrating International Yoga Day in school. (4 marks)

58. Why should we breathe slowly during asanas? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Five
   Panch means five, and there are five great elements.

2. D — Early morning or evening
   Less water dries up in cooler hours.

3. A — Ganga
   The Ganga in India is honoured by many Hindus.

4. A — Lord Mahavir
   Lord Mahavir is believed to have become fully enlightened there.

5. C — Sri Guru Ram Das Ji
   He was the fourth Guru of the Sikhs.

6. A — A man's body with a lion's head and claws
   He is shown as a man-lion.

7. A — Amritsar
   The city that grew into Amritsar.

8. A — The Buddha, the Awakened One
   Siddhartha became the Buddha.

9. A — Langar, the community meal
   Everyone eats together in the langar.

10. A — Sharing lunch with someone who has none
   Sharing with others is a Sikh teaching.

11. C — Practise Ahimsa
   Ahimsa is central in Jainism.

12. C — Not stepping on ants or hurting animals for fun
   Gentleness to living things is central.

13. C — Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   It tells of Ram's fourteen years away from the kingdom.

14. C — A book of wise sayings and verses
   It teaches how to live wisely.

15. B — Gurmukhi
   It is written in Gurmukhi.

16. D — Listen to a resource person or visit a library
   We can listen, read and discuss.

17. A — Fourteen
   Kaikeyi asked that Ram go for fourteen years.

18. D — Daily
   Dainik means daily.

19. C — Sit calmly with hands folded
   Calm sitting is respectful.

20. B — A Hindu place of worship
   A Mandir is a Hindu temple.

21. A — Father
   Pita means father.

22. C — Goddess of knowledge and learning
   Saraswati is the goddess of learning.

23. C — Hinduism
   The Harishchandra story.

24. B — Give it to the driver or conductor
   Returning it shows integrity.

25. A — Not to steal and not to lie
   Not stealing and not lying.

26. A — Not using another's time or ideas without asking
   It includes respecting others' things and ideas.

27. C — An honest carpenter in the Guru Nanak story
   Bhai Lalo earned by honest work.

28. B — On the mat
   The forehead rests on the mat.

29. C — Stretched forward on the floor
   Arms are stretched forward.

30. A — Straight
   A straight back is important.

31. C — Prayer, self-control and forgiveness
   These are its main themes.

32. B — Forgiveness
   Paryushan teaches saying sorry and forgiving.

33. D — February or March
   Phalguna usually falls then.

34. B — May any harm I did be forgiven
   It is a plea for forgiveness.

35. A — They follow the Moon
   The Indian calendar is based on the Moon.

36. D — Sharing with those who cannot afford food or clothes
   We share with the needy.

37. B — Jupiter
   Guru is Jupiter.

38. B — Ravivaar
   Ravi is the Sun.

39. A — Mercury
   Mercury is nearest to the Sun.

40. D — Making a decorated calendar
   Decorating helps memory.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Their lives show courage, kindness and truth. For example, Prahlad's faith and Siddhartha's kindness to the swan. People follow their example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the reason, 2 marks for each example, up to 5.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Daily prayers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for daily and 1 mark for prayers.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prahlad believed God is everywhere, kept praying when his father was angry, and was protected.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kneel with knees together, bring big toes close, sit back on your heels, keep the back and head straight and place palms on the thighs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three correct steps.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: There is one God, all human beings are equal, earn honestly and share with others, and serve without expecting a reward (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Guru Nanak chose to eat at the home of Bhai Lalo, an honest carpenter, instead of Malik Bhago's feast. The lesson is that honest work is the best way to earn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for Bhai Lalo, 1 mark for choosing his home, 1 mark for honest labour, 1 mark for the lesson.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sun, Moon, Mars.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ravivaar: Sun; Somvaar: Moon; Mangalvaar: Mars; Budhvaar: Mercury; Guruvaar: Jupiter; Shukravaar: Venus; Shanivaar: Saturn.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for every two correct pairs, up to 4.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Closing taps, mending leaks, collecting rainwater, reusing water on plants, not polluting rivers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Sun and the Moon.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bal Kaand and Ayodhya Kaand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep promises, respect elders, be humble, do not be greedy for power, love your brothers and sisters, and be courageous (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each lesson.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant bean seeds in two tins of soil. Water one tin every day and give none to the other. Compare them after one and two weeks. The watered seeds sprout and grow but the dry seeds do not.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two tins, 1 mark for different watering, 1 mark for comparing over time, 1 mark for the result.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hindus honour the Ganga and Tulsi; Sikhs remember the Beas and the Ber tree; Jains honour the Rijubalika and the Sal tree; Buddhists honour the Bodhi tree. All value water and trees and take care of them.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each faith correctly described, up to 4 marks, and 1 mark for the idea that all faiths show respect.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mercury is closest to the Sun; Mars is the red planet; Jupiter is the largest; Saturn has rings (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit quietly with a straight back, close eyes and breathe slowly, say it one line at a time and listen first to a teacher or recording so you copy the sounds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three points.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Doing yoga together, taking photos or videos, making a chart of asanas, making a guidance video with an adult (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us calm and helps the body relax.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
